newsitem.title: USA: Ill. corn, bean harvest lags behind normal.
newsitem.headline: Ill. corn, bean harvest lags behind normal.

text.p: Corn and soybean harvest in the week ended Oct. 20 lagged about 10 days behind normal, Illinois' Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop update.
Corn was 35 percent harvested, compared to 73 percent last year and the five-year average of 56 percent. Soybeans were 60 percent harvested, versus 90 percent last year and the average of 86 percent.
Most early crop and soybean harvest was completed and farmers were waiting on late and double crop soybeans to dry down, the report said.
It said rain in the northern districts prevented the corn from drying down.
Corn was 94 percent mature versus 99 percent for the average. The weekly report said 97 percent of soybean plants were dropping leaves, versus an average of 100 percent.

Wheat seeding progressed rapidly in the week, reaching 57 percent complete compared to 78 percent last year and 75 percent for the average. Twenty-two percent was emerged compared 35 percent average, the Illinois crop update said.
Sorghum was 19 percent harvested, compared with 52 percent for the five-year average. The crop was 93 percent mature, matching the five-year average of 93 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent surplus, 67 percent adequate, 28 percent short and four percent very short.
